scenario: A 19-year-old man has glucose of 480 mg/dL, pH 7.15, and large urine ketones. Potassium is 4.8 mEq/L. He is dry. A classmate starts insulin before any fluid and does not plan potassium.
question: What comes before insulin, and why is potassium replaced at 4.8?
options: Bicarbonate as the first drug for pH 7.15
Volume first. The ion will fall
Oral diabetes tablets as the emergency treatment
correctAnswer: Volume first. The ion will fall
citation: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care. 2026.
examTakeaway: Diabetic ketoacidosis is treated with fluids first, then insulin, and potassium is replaced even when the serum number looks normal.
